summary.text: A multiset is like a set in which an element can appear more than once.
The number of times an element occurs is its multiplicity, and the size of a multiset is the sum of the multiplicities of all its elements.
Formally it is a set U together with a function m: U → ℕ that gives each element a nonnegative whole-number multiplicity.

facts.label: Size
facts.value: The sum of all the multiplicities

facts.label: Earliest study
facts.value: Bhaskaracharya, around 1150, on permutations of multisets

facts.label: Coined word
facts.value: Nicolaas de Bruijn coined it in the 1970s, per Knuth

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: Bag, heap, bunch, sample, weighted set and more

facts.label: Equation roots
facts.value: A degree-d equation's complex solutions form a multiset of size d

items.prompt: A quadratic equation has two solutions, and in one case they are the same number. How does a multiset describe that?

options.label: The number is listed once, with multiplicity 2
The number is dropped, since it is repeated
The number is listed once, with multiplicity 1
The equation is said to have no solutions

items.explain: When both solutions are the same number, that number is a solution of multiplicity 2.

items.prompt: A bag holds three red tiles and two blue tiles, treated as a multiset. What is its size?

options.label: 2, the number of colours
3, the larger multiplicity
6, three times two
5, the sum of the multiplicities

items.explain: The size of a multiset is the sum of the multiplicities of all its elements: 3 + 2.

items.prompt: Why can a row of tally marks be thought of as a multiset?

options.label: Because each mark is different from every other mark
Because the marks are treated as indistinguishable, so only how many matters
Because marks in a row are always counted in pairs
Because tally marks were invented after sets

items.explain: Strokes, tally marks and units are considered indistinguishable, so such collections can be regarded as multisets.

items.prompt: A multiset records m(apple) = 3. What does that 3 tell you?

options.label: Apple is the third element in the list
There are three kinds of fruit in it
Apple occurs three times in the multiset
Apple is three times larger than the rest

items.explain: The value m(a) is the multiplicity of a, interpreted as the number of occurrences of a in the multiset.

items.prompt: The lists a, a, b and a, b, b are compared. How do they relate as sets and as multisets?

options.label: Same set, but different multisets
Different sets, but the same multiset
Same set and same multiset
Different sets and different multisets

items.explain: Both lists use the same elements, so they are the same set, but the multiplicities differ, so they are different multisets.

items.prompt: Multisets show up under many names, such as bags and heaps. What explains this?

options.label: Each name was chosen for a different mathematical rule
Practical needs led people to rediscover the idea several times
Mathematicians renamed them whenever the size changed
The names mark multisets of different multiplicities

items.explain: Practical needs for this structure caused multisets to be rediscovered several times under different names.

paragraphs.heading: A set that allows repeats
paragraphs.text: A multiset is a set in which an element may appear more than once. The number of times an element appears is called its multiplicity. Add up the multiplicities of every element and you get the multiset's size. So collections that make up the same set, because they hold the same elements, can still be different multisets.

paragraphs.heading: The formal definition
paragraphs.text: Formally, a multiset is a pair (U, m). Here U is a set, called the universe or underlying set, and m:U → ℕ is a function that gives each element a nonnegative whole number, its multiplicity. The elements whose multiplicity is above zero form the support of the multiset. A multiset with a finite support is called finite, and most authors only use finite ones.

paragraphs.heading: Where multisets show up
paragraphs.text: A very simple and natural example is the multiset made from a natural number's prime factors, with the set of those prime factors as its underlying set. The solutions of an equation give another. A quadratic equation has two solutions, but sometimes both are the same number, which is then a solution of multiplicity 2. More generally, the fundamental theorem of algebra says a polynomial equation of degree d always has complex solutions that form a multiset of size d.

paragraphs.heading: Many names
paragraphs.text: According to Donald Knuth, the word multiset was coined in the 1970s by Nicolaas Govert de Bruijn. Other names have been used for the same idea, including bag, heap, bunch, sample and weighted set. They were important in QA4 and other early AI languages, which called them bags, a term credited to Peter Deutsch.

paragraphs.heading: An ancient idea
paragraphs.text: The idea is far older than the word. Wayne Blizard traced it back to the origin of numbers: in ancient times a number n was often shown as n strokes or tally marks, and since those marks cannot be told apart, such a collection counts as a multiset. The first known study is credited to the Indian mathematician Bhāskarāchārya around 1150, who described permutations of multisets. Jean Prestet published a general rule for such permutations in 1675, and John Wallis explained it in more detail in 1685.

paragraphs.heading: Made precise
paragraphs.text: Richard Dedekind used multisets explicitly in his work. In the 20th century, mathematicians began to treat them as precise mathematical structures. In 1933 Hassler Whitney described generalized sets whose characteristic functions can take any integer value, positive, negative or zero. In 1987 Monro defined a multiset as a set with an equivalence relation linking elements of the same sort, and introduced the multinumber, a function giving the multiplicity of each element.
